<!-- SKELETON DECK — the distinctive ways plants make species. -->

## Learning objectives

By the end you should be able to:

- List the major **modes of plant speciation** and their genomic signatures.
- Explain why **polyploidy** and **hybridization** make plants special.
- Connect reproductive-isolation barriers to earlier popgen concepts.

# Isolating barriers {.center}

## Pre- and post-zygotic isolation

- **Prezygotic:** phenology, pollinator, habitat, mechanical, gametic (placeholder).
- **Postzygotic:** hybrid inviability/sterility; Bateson–Dobzhansky–Muller incompatibilities.
- Isolation is usually **multi-dimensional and incomplete** in plants.

# Modes of speciation {.center}

## The plant speciation toolkit

- **Polyploidy / hybrid speciation** — instantaneous reproductive isolation via WGD
  (allo-/autopolyploidy). <span class="xref">→ popgen deck 06; genome architecture (Nov 10).</span>
- **Pollinator shifts** — floral trait change → assortative mating (e.g. *Mimulus*, orchids).
- **Mating-system shifts** — selfing as an isolating + diversification factor
  <span class="xref">(popgen deck 03)</span>.
- **Chromosomal** — rearrangements, aneuploidy.
- **Ecological / divergent selection** — soils, elevation, climate
  <span class="xref">(popgen deck 05)</span>.

## Speciation with gene flow

- Divergence despite ongoing gene flow; "genomic islands of divergence."
- Sets up **adaptive introgression** <span class="xref">(Oct 8)</span> and species networks
  <span class="xref">(Oct 15)</span>.

## Summary

- Plants speciate via **polyploidy, hybridization, pollinator/mating-system shifts,
  chromosomal, and ecological** routes — often with gene flow.
- Reproductive isolation is typically **multifarious and porous**.
